title: Cut-off times and NAV applicability
objectives: Explain which day's NAV a purchase or redemption gets.
State why the time funds are available matters.
Tell a client what to expect for a late-day order.
body_md:
The NAV a client gets depends on **when the request is received and when the money is available**, not simply when the client pressed the button.

## Cut-off times

| Order | General rule for most schemes |
|---|---|
| Purchase (not liquid or overnight) | Received and funds available before 3:00 pm on a business day gets that day's NAV |
| Redemption | Received before 3:00 pm on a business day gets that day's NAV |
| Liquid and overnight purchase | Earlier cut-off, with funds available for use before 1:30 pm |
| After the cut-off, or on a holiday | Next business day's NAV |

<!-- TODO-VERIFY: cut-off times and the funds-availability rule per the latest SEBI circular on uniform cut-off timings; confirm before each training cycle. -->

## Why availability matters

For most non-liquid schemes, the NAV applied to a purchase is that of the day the money is available for use in the scheme. A cheque or transfer that clears the next day gets the next day's NAV. Online payments that settle instantly usually get the same-day NAV if made before the cut-off.

## SIPs and switches

A SIP instalment gets the NAV of the SIP date if funds are available, or the next business day if the date is a holiday. A switch is treated as a redemption from one scheme and a purchase in another, each with its own cut-off.

> **Investor takeaway:** Timing decides the NAV, so place orders early and keep funds ready.
example: A client submits a redemption at 3:20 pm on Tuesday. It misses the 3:00 pm cut-off, so it gets Wednesday's NAV. If Wednesday's market falls, the client receives less than Tuesday's NAV would have paid.
say: Orders in by 3 pm get that day's NAV. After that, it is the next business day's.
The NAV depends on when the money reaches the fund, not only when you click.
never: You will definitely get today's NAV.
Late orders still get today's price.

check.q: A redemption request in a non-liquid scheme is received at 3:20 pm on Tuesday. Which NAV applies?
check.why: After the 3:00 pm cut-off the next business day's NAV applies.

check.q: A client pays by a transfer that clears the next day. Which NAV does a non-liquid scheme purchase generally get?
o: The day the order was placed
The day the funds are available for use
check.why: NAV generally follows the day funds become available for use in the scheme.

check.q: A switch from Fund A to Fund B is treated as:
o: A single transaction with no NAV
A transfer of units at cost
check.why: A switch is a redemption plus a purchase, each at its own applicable NAV.
